Today's Talking Points: Gotta get a message to you After the flurry of major central bank decisions over the last 10 days comes the even bigger flurry of policymaker speeches, interviews, and media appearances. Do market expectations move all that much from where they were the day of these decisions and press conferences by chiefs Warsh, Lagarde, Ueda and Bailey? Not really, because the general consensus views and likely policy paths, such as they exist, have already been laid out. There are 19 Fed policymakers (although only 12 voters at any one time), and 27 ECB rate-setters - that's a lot of commentary for investors to ignore. The BoE and BOJ's nine-strong policymaking committees are positively lean by comparison. Investors are more likely to take their lead in the coming days from elsewhere - fresh economic data, corporate developments, geopolitics, Middle East energy supply shifts. Oil slick Global oil prices are back below $100 a barrel, with Brent and WTI crude futures falling on Tuesday for a fifth straight day. That's the longest downward streak for both benchmarks in over a year. Could the market be at a turning point? Has the second oil shock of the Iran war come and gone? It would probably be unwise to be too confident, but [USN:L8N45E0CI TEXT:"a peace deal in the offing"] and more supply potentially coming back onto the market could have a significant impact. All that is hypothetical right now. Oil is still up 50% from a year ago, and analysts estimate that up to half of the US inflation overshoot is down to elevated energy and commodity prices. But a sustained decline would wipe much of that away, and call into question the recent strengthening of market rate hike expectations - and policymaker signaling - across much of the developed world. Disunited Nations The United Nations General Assembly is in full flow, with nearly 130 world leaders gathered in New York. That's not a great turnout, which may reflect the old world order of multilateralism, globalization and cross-border cooperation gradually giving way to one characterized more by nationalism, bilateral agreements and de-globalization. The biggest 'no-show' is Chinese President Xi Jinping, who will meet Trump in Washington later this week. Trump addressed the UN assembly today (prompting a walkout by the Cuban delegation), and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres gave his final address, in which he called for greater curbs on AI. One wonders how many world leaders will be showing up at the annual jamboree in 5 or 10 years' time (presuming AI hasn't wiped out mankind by then). What could move markets tomorrow? item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros do cacau se recuperaram nesta terça-feira, após atingirem mínimas de sete semanas e meia no início do pregão, enquanto o açúcar bruto também voltou a subir, depois de cair para uma mínima de 4 semanas. CACAU * O cacau de Londres fechou com alta de £37, ou 0,9%, a £3.998 por tonelada métrica. O mercado havia registrado, anteriormente, uma mínima de 7 semanas e meia, de £3.799. * Os corretores afirmaram que a recente fraqueza foi impulsionada pelo excesso de oferta, embora se espere um mercado mais equilibrado na safra de 2026/27, com a produção global prevista para cair. * A precipitação ficou abaixo da média na semana passada na maioria das principais regiões produtoras de cacau da Costa do Marfim, e os agricultores afirmaram na segunda-feira que as condições de seca poderiam ameaçar o desenvolvimento das pequenas vagens que devem ser colhidas no próximo ano, durante a safra principal, que vai de setembro a fevereiro. * O contrato futuro de cacau de Nova York subiu 1%, para US$5.402 por tonelada, após atingir uma mínima de 7 semanas e meia, de US$ 5.111. AÇÚCAR * O açúcar bruto fechou com alta de 0,11 centavo, ou 0,6%, a 17,59 centavos por libra-peso, após atingir uma mínima de 4 semanas de 17,11 centavos. * Operadores afirmaram que a retração do mercado em relação à máxima de 16 meses de 18,88 centavos, registrada em 10 de setembro, ainda pode se aprofundar, embora as perspectivas sejam mais positivas no médio a longo prazo, com o fenômeno climático El Niño previsto para prejudicar a produção e, potencialmente, levar a um déficit global na safra de 2026/27. * O preço do açúcar branco permaneceu praticamente inalterado em US$507,90 por tonelada, após atingir uma mínima de US$496,80, a menor cotação em 6 semanas e meia. CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou em queda de 4,1 centavos, ou 1,5%, a US$2,723 por libra-peso, após atingir uma mínima de três meses de US$ 2,7130. * Os corretores afirmaram que as condições climáticas favoráveis à safra nos principais países produtores, Brasil e Vietnã, contribuíram para a recente desvalorização. * Eles observaram, no entanto, que a atividade no mercado físico no Brasil começou a ser afetada, já que os produtores se abstiveram de vender mais grãos aos preços atuais. * O café robusta recuou 2,3%, para US$3.260 a tonelada. O mercado havia atingido, anteriormente, uma mínima de mais de três meses, de US$ 3.245. (Reportagem de Nigel Hunt e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: EQT sees higher 2026 US natgas output on lower spending, CEO says
item.description: EQT , the second-biggest US natural gas producer, plans to pull more gas out of the ground in 2026 while spending less money than last year to meet growing global demand, CEO Toby Rice told Reuters on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Scott Disavino
item.content:encoded: EQT (EQT.N) , the second-biggest US natural gas producer, plans to pull more gas out of the ground in 2026 while spending less money than last year to meet growing global demand, CEO Toby Rice told Reuters on Tuesday. He said record production will come despite curtailed production in recent months by EQT and others in the Marcellus and Utica shale regions of Pennsylvania, Ohio and West Virginia. The producers are waiting for gas prices in the region to rise. "We have a shut-in program. During times of low prices, we sell less. When prices are higher, we sell more," Rice said. "Having a business that's able to throttle the production aligned with what the market requires ... is one of the reasons we've been able to beat our pricing expectations," Rice said. He said EQT has benefited by a little over $200 million a year from its ability to sell less gas when prices are low and more when prices are high. In its second-quarter earnings in July, EQT (EQT.N) reduced 2026 maintenance capital spending guidance by $25 million to a range of $2.040 billion to $2.190 billion. It boosted its production guidance for the year by 0.25 billion cubic feet of gas equivalent per day (bcfed) to an average of 6.5 to 6.7 bcfed. That compares with spending of of around $2.324 billion in 2025 to produce an average of 6.5 bcfed. One billion cubic feet is enough gas to supply about five million US homes for a day. On average, the US consumed a record 91.9 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) of gas in 2025 and exported a record 24.6 bcfd as liquefied natural gas to the world or via pipelines to Mexico and Canada, according to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA). The EIA and other analysts expect US gas use to keep hitting record highs in coming years as demand surges to power data centers and for export as LNG and by pipeline. NEW OPORTUNITES "We're really pushing to find ways to expand demand for Appalachian molecules," Rice said. In August, EQT launched an open season for its proposed POWER pipeline project to move up to 1.0 bcfd of gas about 50 miles (80 kilometers) from Pennsylvania to Ohio, where several firms plan to build or expand power-hungry data centers running artificial intelligence. EQT told prospective customers the pipe could enter service in January 2030 and Rice said the POWER pipe could move more than 1.0 bcfd depending on demand. In addition to the proposed POWER pipe, EQT has been expanding its 2.0-bcfd Mountain Valley Pipeline from West Virginia to Virginia. That project, known as MVP Boost, is on track to add about 0.6 bcfd of capacity to the mainline in 2028. The MVP Southgate project is on track to start moving about 0.55 bcfd of gas from Virginia to North Carolina starting in late 2026. On Monday, EQT signed a 10-year deal to supply about one LNG cargo per year to Lithuania's majority state-owned energy firm Ignitis. "We're incredibly bullish on the international markets," Rice said. He said EQT sees gas demand growing through 2040 by around 20 bcfd in domestic markets and by around 200 bcfd in international markets. EQT will have about 6 million tonnes per year of LNG (roughly 0.8 bcfd of gas) available to sell around 2030-2031 when some LNG export plants under construction and development enter service, including NextDecade's (NEXT.O) Rio Grande in Texas, Sempra's (SRE.N) Port Arthur in Texas and Caturus' Commonwealth in Louisiana. That is about 15% of the company's gas portfolio.

item.title: Black Foils focus on future after tough SailGP season
item.description: Black Foils co-CEO Blair Tuke said the New Zealand team are building for the future, including protecting the oceans fundamental to their sport, as they near the end of what he said had been a "really tough" SailGP season.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Smith
item.content:encoded: Black Foils co-CEO Blair Tuke said the New Zealand team are building for the future, including protecting the oceans fundamental to their sport, as they near the end of what he said had been a "really tough" SailGP season. A [USN:L4N3ZC07T TEXT:"high-speed crash"] with France in front of New Zealand's home crowd in February resulted in the team's sailors being shore bound for months and [USN:L4N3ZE0XE TEXT:"missing"] four events while SailGP built a replacement for their F50 catamaran, which was beyond repair. "It's been a really tough one is probably the only way to put it. We had four months when we didn't sail or race as a team," Tuke told Reuters in a recent interview. "It's a mix now. We're obviously trying to build for next season and develop, but probably the best way to do that is to try and put your best foot forward and to race well and put yourselves under pressure," the 37-year-old wing trimmer added. With no prospect of reaching November's grand final in Abu Dhabi, the team are also working on developing new talent. "The season's out of reach," Tuke said, adding that Black Foils, who now lie 12th on the season leaderboard, were aiming to "win race weekends and build processes and experience that sets us up for the future". Tuke is a fan of the new group racing format that splits SailGP's now 13-strong fleet in two, partly as a precaution aimed at avoiding clashes like the dramatic one in Auckland. "It had to happen at some point as SailGP grew and I think following some of the incidents that happened earlier this year it maybe got fast-tracked a little quicker," he said. 'MUCH BIGGER THAN OURSELVES' Tuke said New York-based MSP Sports Capital's [USN:L8N42R0OS TEXT:"acquisition of a majority stake"] in the Black Foils gives them a "really exciting opportunity", both on and off the water. "We're so focused on becoming a global sports brand that represents New Zealand on the world stage, that pushes what's possible on the performance side," said Tuke, adding that the team is also targeting "something much bigger than ourselves". Having MSP's backing has 'supercharged' the team's ability to achieve all those things, said Tuke, partly with reference to the Live Ocean Foundation he founded with co-CEO and longtime sailing partner Pete Burling in late 2019. "The ocean is declining fast and its health is key to our future on this planet," Tuke said of the campaigns which Live Ocean has launched in New Zealand to "bring people round to issues they otherwise wouldn't be made aware of". "We've got the platform in sport to do something," he said, adding that he and Burling had wanted to be able to integrate their campaigning into something that they did every day. For Tuke, establishing the team's Live Ocean partnership was a "non-negotiable" in discussions with SailGP, which runs its own impact league among teams, from the outset. "I am very committed to making sure we leave this place in a better state than when I came into it," he said.

item.title: Petróleo fecha em baixa com melhora no fluxo no Oriente Médio
item.description: Os preços do petróleo caíram nesta terça-feira devido ao aumento do fluxo do produto saudita com a retomada das operações do oleoduto Leste-Oeste e dos tráfegos marítimos pelo Estreito de Ormuz, por onde passavam 20% do abastecimento global antes do início da guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, no final de fevereiro.
item.dc:creator: Erwin Seba
item.content:encoded: Os preços do petróleo caíram nesta terça-feira devido ao aumento do fluxo do produto saudita com a retomada das operações do oleoduto Leste-Oeste e dos tráfegos marítimos pelo Estreito de Ormuz, por onde passavam 20% do abastecimento global antes do início da guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, no final de fevereiro. O Brent e o petróleo dos EUA recuperaram parte das perdas mais acentuadas do dia depois que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, frustrou as esperanças de que um acordo fosse alcançado em breve, ao afirmar que um acordo de paz só seria firmado após as eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA, no início de novembro. Trump também afirmou que, sem um acordo de paz, poderia "aniquilar" o Irã. Esperava-se que Trump se reunisse com líderes mundiais na ONU, em Nova York, nesta semana, alimentando esperanças de estabilidade no Oriente Médio e talvez até mesmo de avanços para pôr fim à guerra de quatro anos e meio da Rússia na Ucrânia. O contrato futuro do Brent fechou a US$99,25 o barril, com queda de US$1,09, ou 1,09%. O contrato outubro do petróleo WTI , que vence nesta terça-feira, fechou a US$94,99 o barril, com queda de US$1,19, ou 1,24%. Em suas mínimas da sessão, ambas as referências chegaram a cair mais de US$2 por barril. Em seguida, os comentários de Trump frustraram as crescentes esperanças de que um acordo pudesse ser alcançado durante a reunião da Assembleia Geral da ONU, realizada esta semana em Nova York. Alimentando o otimismo, observou-se um aumento no fluxo de tráfego pelo Estreito de Ormuz nos últimos dias. "A Arábia Saudita está agindo, não esperando", disse Phil Flynn, analista sênior da Price Futures Group. "Depois que ataques dos houthis ao oleoduto Leste-Oeste forçaram a interrupção dos carregamentos em Yanbu, a Aramco carregou cerca de 14 milhões de barris de petróleo bruto em sete superpetroleiros (VLCCs) dentro do Golfo Pérsico. Dados de satélite e rastreadores mostraram que o petróleo saudita que passou pelo Estreito de Ormuz atingiu uma média de cerca de 2,9 milhões de barris por dia nos últimos seis dias, um aumento em relação aos cerca de 700 mil barris por dia registrados em agosto." A Arábia Saudita reiniciou as operações em seu oleoduto Leste-Oeste e poderá retomar as exportações pelo porto de Yanbu ainda nesta terça-feira, afirmaram três fontes a par do assunto. O Irã pode reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz em até sete dias se os EUA aliviarem a pressão militar e suspenderem o bloqueio aos portos iranianos, disse uma alta autoridade iraniana à Reuters nesta terça-feira. A autoridade afirmou que a delegação iraniana na Assembleia Geral da ONU, em Nova York, tem plena autoridade para retomar as negociações diplomáticas com os EUA.

item.title: Microsoft concederá à Darpa acesso direto a sistema de computação quântica nos EUA
item.description: A Microsoft anunciou nesta terça-feira que concederá à Agência de Projetos de Pesquisa Avançada de Defesa dos Estados Unidos (DARPA) acesso direto ao seu mais recente hardware de computação quântica, como parte de um novo centro de pesquisa que a empresa inaugurou no estado norte-americano de Maryland.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: A Microsoft (MSFT.O) anunciou nesta terça-feira que concederá à Agência de Projetos de Pesquisa Avançada de Defesa dos Estados Unidos (DARPA) acesso direto ao seu mais recente hardware de computação quântica, como parte de um novo centro de pesquisa que a empresa inaugurou no estado norte-americano de Maryland. O centro, localizado próximo a Washington, D.C., abrigará um novo sistema quântico que utiliza o chip Majorana 2 da Microsoft para testes e avaliações independentes pela Darpa. Os computadores quânticos prometem resolver problemas que levariam milhares de anos para serem resolvidos por máquinas convencionais. Um tema de particular interesse para especialistas em segurança nacional é a proteção e a quebra de comunicações criptografadas. A Microsoft é uma das várias empresas de computação quântica que estão sendo avaliadas pela Darpa para descobrir se alguma abordagem de computação quântica pode resultar em sistemas economicamente viáveis até 2033. Até agora, a Darpa avaliava a tecnologia da Microsoft remotamente, acessando máquinas em Redmond, Washington, e na Europa. A instalação em Maryland marca uma mudança para o acesso físico em um espaço dedicado da Darpa, onde seus especialistas podem operar o hardware por meio de suas próprias sequências de inicialização. “Isso é muito importante para nós porque, essencialmente, permite que a Darpa teste a máquina e avalie o quão boa ela é e como está se saindo”, disse Zulfi Alam, vice-presidente corporativo da Microsoft Quantum, em entrevista. Alam disse que o acordo impõe disciplina à medida que a Microsoft passa da fase de pesquisa para o desenvolvimento de um produto comercial. A principal métrica de avaliação da Darpa é se o valor do cálculo realizado por um sistema quântico supera o custo do sistema. “Isso impõe um certo rigor de engenharia que as equipes científicas normalmente não têm”, disse ele, descrevendo a Darpa como “uma organização totalmente confiável” com a qual a Microsoft pode compartilhar tanto o trabalho atual quanto os planos futuros. Alam disse que a Darpa começará com o chip Majorana 2, mas que o sistema em Maryland será construído para poder receber futuros chips que a Microsoft está desenvolvendo. A Microsoft afirmou que planeja ter sistemas quânticos comerciais prontos até 2029.

item.title: Apollo private credit fund redemption requests ease in third quarter
item.description: Asset manager Apollo Global Management recorded lower withdrawal requests at its flagship private credit fund in the third-quarter tender offer, suggesting redemption queues are beginning to clear.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Asset manager Apollo Global Management (APO.N) recorded lower withdrawal requests at its flagship private credit fund in the third-quarter tender offer, suggesting redemption queues are beginning to clear. Investors in Apollo Debt Solutions BDC (ADS) sought to withdraw roughly 14.7% of shares in the latest tender offer, compared with 16.8% in the prior quarter, according to a regulatory filing on Tuesday. The $25.9 billion fund will repurchase 5% of shares, the customary threshold for such vehicles. The Apollo fund said repurchase requests declined sequentially across both US onshore and offshore investors, and most of them were investors resubmitting unfulfilled requests from prior quarters. Demand from wealth investors to pull money from private credit funds hit record levels this year on concerns about lending standards and AI disruption risks. However, redemption pressure has recently begun to ease across major non-traded private credit funds as asset managers work through a backlog of unfulfilled withdrawal requests and sentiment improves after a turbulent period. Earlier this month, BlackRock (BLK.N) also [USN:L4N4530XC TEXT:"revealed a decline in redemption requests"] at its private credit funds. Most non-traded private credit funds have enforced the customary 5% limit on redemptions this year, keeping withdrawal requests elevated as investors resubmit their unfulfilled requests in following tender offers. "Following third-quarter repurchase payments, investors who have sought liquidity during 2026 will have received an estimated 75% of their requested capital," the Apollo fund said. During the quarter, ADS received $0.2 billion in gross subscriptions through September 1. Quarterly net outflows are expected to be roughly $0.5 billion, or 3% of net asset value. Since inception, ADS' Class I shares have delivered a net total return of 8.2% as of August 31, outperforming leveraged loan and high-yield markets by 177 and 377 basis points, respectively. Data from major vehicles run by Ares (ARES.N) and Blue Owl (OWL.N) are expected in coming weeks.

item.title: Financial stocks fall with AI and flattening yield curve in focus
item.description: The S&P 500 Financial index and the benchmark's bank sector were under pressure on Tuesday as investors worried about competition from artificial intelligence and uncertainty around AI-related initial public offerings, along with moves in the bond market that potentially point to softer conditions ahead.
item.dc:creator: Sinead Carew
item.content:encoded: The S&P 500 Financial index (.SPSY) and the benchmark's bank sector (.SPXBK) were under pressure on Tuesday as investors worried about competition from artificial intelligence and uncertainty around AI-related initial public offerings, along with moves in the bond market that potentially point to softer conditions ahead. The benchmark's broader financial index finished down 2% on Tuesday with money managers Charles Schwab (SCHW.N) , Ameriprise Financial (AMP.N) and Raymond James (RJF.N) among the biggest decliners. Schwab fell 6.1% while Ameriprise shares fell 4.4% and Raymond James shares lost more than 3%. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 bank index finished down 3%. With Muse, an AI agent from Meta Platforms (META.O) , recently moving past ChatGPT as the most downloaded free app for iPhones , Macrae Sykes, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds, said that investors have started to become concerned about potential competition from the app in the wealth management industry. "There's worries about AI disruption to traditional businesses," said Sykes, who manages investments in the financial industry. "Clearly there's going to be some arguments both around the benefits and the disruption of AI tools and what it all means for the incumbents, but I think today is another sell-without-regard reaction." Sykes also highlighted moves in the US bond market where the yield curve between short- and long-dated bonds has been flattening, which could eat into bank returns. A closely watched part of the Treasury [USN:L6N45E0RQ TEXT:"yield curve"] measuring the gap between yields on two- and 10-year Treasury notes , seen as an indicator of the health of economic expectations, hit its flattest level since March 2025 earlier on Tuesday. It was last at a positive 21 basis points but was as low as 17.90 basis points earlier on Tuesday. As traders have increased their bets on Federal Reserve rate hikes, the curve, which was at 55.5 on August 18, has been flattening gradually. "There's a tipping point between raising rates reflecting a strong economy and raising rates and having the effect of slowing the economy," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments, a family investment office in New Vernon, New Jersey. Gabelli's Sykes also pointed to concerns about the market for initial public offerings after a New York Times report on Monday about delays in initial public offerings for companies tied to the data centers supporting AI. [USN:L4N44T0VL TEXT:"SB Energy"], a subsidiary of the Japanese conglomerate SoftBank (9984.T) , filed paperwork recently for a US IPO. But the data center developer, which had originally planned an IPO for this month, has postponed the launch of its roadshow to market the offering to investors, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters. SB Energy declined to comment. Nuclear services company [USN:L4N4581N6 TEXT:"Holtec"] last week suspended its planned US IPO. Still, Sykes argues that the outlook for bank stocks is strong. "The short-term noise does not affect our appreciation for the long-term outlook," he said. "The outlook in general for banks is pretty good. There's a good economy and good employment. The fundamentals are good."

item.title: WPP finance chief Joanne Wilson to become Diageo CFO, Sky News reports
item.description: WPP CFO Joanne Wilson is set to leave Britain's biggest advertising group to become finance chief of Guinness-maker Diageo , Sky News reported on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: WPP (WPP.L) CFO Joanne Wilson is set to leave Britain's biggest advertising group to become finance chief of Guinness-maker Diageo (DGE.L) , Sky News reported on Tuesday. Diageo was finalising Wilson's appointment and could announce the move as early as Wednesday, the report said. Diageo declined to comment, while WPP did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside regular business hours. The move comes as Diageo undergoes a broad overhaul under CEO Dave Lewis, who last month [USN:L4N4430TT TEXT:"unveiled"] a $1 billion cost-cutting plan, saying the world's largest spirits maker must adapt to a prolonged period of weak growth. Lewis is reshaping the company's management and board, while implementing a restructuring programme that has already led to the departure of several senior executives and reductions in headcount. Wilson would replace Nik Jhangiani, who is expected to leave the spirits maker, according to Sky News. Jhangiani, who [USN:L4N3H651J TEXT:"joined"] Diageo as CFO in May 2024 and later became interim CEO, [USN:L1N3TE0FB TEXT:"won praise"] from investors for his communication style and leadership, with some shareholders backing him as a candidate for the chief executive role. The move would also reunite Wilson with Lewis, a former colleague from her time at Tesco (TSCO.L) . Meanwhile, Wilson's departure from WPP comes as the British advertising group navigates a leadership transition and seeks to improve its performance after a period of weaker growth relative to some industry peers.

item.title: Dodgers bolster roster, return CF Andy Pages, RHP Roki Sasaki from IL
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers activated a pair of key contributors in advance of a marquee series against the San Diego Padres, bringing back center fielder Andy Pages and right-hander Roki Sasaki from the injured list.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Dodgers activated a pair of key contributors in advance of a marquee series against the San Diego Padres, bringing back center fielder Andy Pages and right-hander Roki Sasaki from the injured list. In corresponding moves, right-hander Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City. Pages, 25, has not played since Aug. 21, when he was hit by a pitch on the left hand from Pittsburgh Pirates right-hander Bubba Chandler. An All-Star for the first time this season, Pages was batting .272 with 21 home runs and 80 RBIs in 128 games. Sasaki, 24, last pitched Aug. 26 when he developed a blister on his right middle finger in an outing against the Atlanta Braves. He is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA in 23 outings (all starts) this season and is scheduled to make an abbreviated appearance Tuesday. Sheehan, 26, started the season in the Los Angeles rotation, was sent down in early August amid ongoing struggles and has returned for three outings this month where he recorded 24 strikeouts over 17 innings. He is 5-8 with a 4.57 ERA in 23 appearances (22 starts) this season. Sheehan and Sasaki both are projected to have a bullpen role for the Dodgers in the playoffs, according to manager Dave Roberts. Alfonzo, 26, made his major league debut in July and is batting .179 with four RBIs in 13 career games. While the Dodgers enter Tuesday's play with a magic number of three to clinch a bye into a National League Division Series matchup, the Padres have a magic number of two to clinch a wild-card spot and a team-record third consecutive playoff appearance. Also on Tuesday, the Dodgers sold Ryan Ward's contract to the Chunichi Dragons in Japan, according to multiple reports. A longtime minor leaguer, the 28-year-old Ward made his major league debut this season and hit three home runs in 20 games. The former Pacific Coast League MVP was designated for assignment last week. --Field Level Media

item.title: Boeing e GoGo testam drone militar conectado via satélite em desafio à Starlink
item.description: A Insitu, subsidiária da Boeing especializada em drones, e a Gogo, provedora de WiFi para aviação, testaram com sucesso um drone militar utilizando comunicações via satélite, informaram as empresas nesta terça-feira, destacando os esforços crescentes de governos e empresas de produtos militares para reduzir a dependência da Starlink, do bilionário Elon Musk.
item.dc:creator: Mike Stone
item.content:encoded: A Insitu, subsidiária da Boeing (BA.N) especializada em drones, e a Gogo, provedora de WiFi para aviação, testaram com sucesso um drone militar utilizando comunicações via satélite, informaram as empresas nesta terça-feira, destacando os esforços crescentes de governos e empresas de produtos militares para reduzir a dependência da Starlink, do bilionário Elon Musk. A Gogo Special Missions, braço militar e governamental da Gogo (GOGO.O) , e a Insitu integraram uma versão modificada da antena Galileo HDX da Gogo ao drone Integrator da Insitu, uma aeronave não tripulada de médio porte utilizada por clientes militares para missões de vigilância e reconhecimento. Ataques com drones tornaram-se fundamentais para a estratégia militar após seu uso generalizado na guerra da Rússia na Ucrânia e em conflitos em todo o Oriente Médio. À medida que as forças armadas buscam operar drones em alcances maiores, resistir a ataques de interferência e realizar missões cada vez mais complexas, elas estão recorrendo a redes de satélites, como a Starlink. A Gogo e a Insitu afirmaram que seu sistema fornece ao drone Integrator internet global de alta velocidade por meio da rede de satélites de órbita baixa da Eutelsat (ETL.PA) OneWeb e não está sujeito ao Regulamento de Tráfico Internacional de Armas (ITAR) dos EUA, facilitando exportações para clientes internacionais. “Adicionar uma opção de SATCOM de alta velocidade isenta das regras do ITAR é um recurso essencial para nossos clientes globais”, afirmou John Kelly, vice-presidente de crescimento da Insitu, em comunicado, acrescentando que a tecnologia ampliará o alcance de comando e controle e permitirá uma transmissão mais rápida dos dados dos sensores do campo de batalha. A Gogo e a Insitu não divulgaram um cronograma para a implantação do sistema. A serviços Starlink e Starshield, o produto seguro de comunicações via satélite da SpaceX voltado para governos, aos usuários militares tornou-se uma importante fonte de receita para a empresa de Musk. No entanto, governos europeus e alguns setores do Pentágono têm manifestado preocupações quanto à dependência excessiva do Starlink, cuja constelação de milhares de satélites supera em muito a de seus concorrentes.

item.title: US Supreme Court denies surrogate's bid to block California parentage ruling
item.description: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to halt a judicial ruling declaring a California couple the legal parents of an infant born to their surrogate who refused their request to terminate the pregnancy after the fetus was diagnosed with a severe cardiac defect and later sought a role in decisions affecting the boy's medical care.
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday declined to halt a judicial ruling declaring a California couple the legal parents of an infant born to their surrogate who refused their request to terminate the pregnancy after the fetus was diagnosed with a severe cardiac defect and later sought a role in decisions affecting the boy's medical care. The court denied a request by McKenna West, the woman hired by Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed to serve as a surrogate, to block the ruling by a California court while she appeals the matter to the Supreme Court. The order was issued unilaterally by Justice Elena Kagan, who handles emergency cases arising from California and other states in the region. Kagan provided no rationale. West refused the couple's request to terminate the pregnancy after the cardiac diagnosis and gave birth to the baby on August 12 in Dallas. The couple sued West for breach of their surrogacy agreement, including her refusal to terminate the pregnancy. West challenged the state of California's authority to declare the couple the child's legal parents. She previously sought custody of the boy and has pursued a role in decisions about his medical care. The baby, as of last Friday, had remained in a Texas hospital, where he is receiving treatment, the couple's lawyer said. The couple in Supreme Court papers last Friday argued that they are committed to the same lifesaving care that West has said she wants for the boy. After the dispute arose, a California trial court in June ruled that Gilkar and Ahmed were the legal parents, rejecting West's contention that the court lacked jurisdiction over her, and state appellate courts declined to stay that decision. This prompted West's request to the Supreme Court. In a filing, West's lawyers argued that the Supreme Court's intervention was needed because the California judicial ruling was being enforced in Texas, leaving her without authority over the child amid decisions about his medical care. West is represented by lawyers from the conservative legal advocacy group Alliance Defending Freedom. The group has been involved in anti-abortion litigation including the Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization case in which the Supreme Court in 2022 overturned its 1973 Roe v. Wade landmark that had legalized abortion nationwide. Republican Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who is running for a US Senate seat, backed West at an earlier stage of the case.

item.title: Jefe BID busca 2.500 millones de dólares para Venezuela; consejeros se resisten: fuentes
item.description: El presidente del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) ha estado trabajando para obtener la aprobación de un préstamo de 2.500 millones de dólares para Venezuela, pero se ha enfrentado a la oposición de algunos miembros del consejo de administración de la entidad, dijeron a Reuters dos fuentes con conocimiento del asunto.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos, Cassandra Garrison
item.content:encoded: El presidente del Banco Interamericano de Desarrollo (BID) ha estado trabajando para obtener la aprobación de un préstamo de 2.500 millones de dólares para Venezuela, pero se ha enfrentado a la oposición de algunos miembros del consejo de administración de la entidad, dijeron a Reuters dos fuentes con conocimiento del asunto. El presidente del BID, Ilan Goldfajn, ha enfrentado inquietudes de la junta sobre la posibilidad de otorgar un crédito a Caracas sin la habitual labor paralela de otros prestamistas multilaterales, a pesar de que la junta reconoce los beneficios de retomar la relación con Venezuela, señaló una de las fuentes. El BID dejó de otorgar nuevos préstamos al país sudamericano en mayo de 2018 después de que este se retrasó en los pagos. Estos esfuerzos ponen de manifiesto los desafíos que enfrenta Venezuela para resolver sus problemas de deuda. El país exportador de petróleo atraviesa una crisis de liquidez y macroeconómica que combina, entre otros factores, ingresos petroleros mucho menores y un déficit fiscal creciente. Se prevé que la reestructuración de su deuda —que según algunas estimaciones podría superar los 200.000 millones de dólares— sea compleja y lenta. Una operación del BID por 2.500 millones de dólares sería significativa como financiación para una etapa inicial de recuperación, pero representa una cifra insignificante frente al problema estructural del balance financiero de Venezuela. La concreción de dicho préstamo requeriría superar varios obstáculos. Actualmente, el BID no puede otorgar préstamos a Venezuela debido a su política sobre atrasos en pagos públicos, dado que Caracas adeuda más de 2.000 millones de dólares en capital e intereses vencidos al organismo regional. No obstante, dichos atrasos podrían saldarse mediante un préstamo puente de un tercero, un procedimiento habitual para reintegrar a un país en el sistema financiero internacional, indicó una de las fuentes. El BID declinó hacer comentarios y el gobierno venezolano no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios. El préstamo propuesto se enmarcaría en un mecanismo de Préstamo Especial para el Desarrollo (SDL, por sus siglas en inglés), el cual, en el caso de Venezuela, tendría un límite de 500 millones de dólares conforme a las normas del BID, dijeron las fuentes. Un préstamo de 2.500 millones de dólares a Caracas requeriría una excepción respecto al monto máximo permitido, así como una segunda excepción por la ausencia de un programa vigente con el Fondo Monetario Internacional, requisito este último para los préstamos SDL, según la normativa del banco. Goldfajn [USN:L6N45818S TEXT:"declaró"] a Reuters el lunes que el BID trabaja en una "nota de acercamiento" con Venezuela, un plan a corto plazo que suele preceder a la concesión de nuevos préstamos. Cualquier propuesta de préstamo a Venezuela requeriría, en última instancia, la aprobación del Directorio Ejecutivo del BID —integrado por 14 miembros—, donde Estados Unidos ostenta el 30% del poder de voto, seguido por Argentina y Brasil, con un 11% y 35% cada uno. El BID cuenta con 48 países miembros, incluidos 26 países prestatarios de América Latina y el Caribe, región donde constituye la principal fuente de financiación multilateral. En 2025, aprobó nuevos préstamos y garantías por valor de 17.400 millones de dólares, mientras que su cartera de préstamos pendientes alcanzó casi 118.000 millones de dólares, según su informe anual más reciente.

item.title: Market participants favor Treasury parking some cash in repo market
item.description: The idea of the US Treasury periodically investing some of its cash into private money markets got a favorable hearing at a panel of market participants held by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: The idea of the US Treasury periodically investing some of its cash into private money markets got a favorable hearing at a panel of market participants held by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York on Tuesday. “At a high level, the Treasury reinvesting into repo makes sense,” said Richard Chambers, a partner at Goldman Sachs’ banking and markets group, in comments made while speaking on a panel held as part of the regional central bank’s annual Treasury market conference. “It makes sense from a debt sustainability perspective” to have the “largest” debt issuer in the world help stabilize a money market sector that helps investors and traders get involved with government bonds, he said. “Having new cash enter the market does add ballast” to money markets, said Frank Gutierrez, head of portfolio management and trading at BNY Investments Dreyfus. Private repo markets are critical for fixed-income bond trading, vast in size and involve participants borrowing and lending cash and Treasuries to facilitate their trading positions. The New York Fed panel was exploring the possibility, first broached in [USN:L1N41J0ZR TEXT:"May"], that the Treasury may periodically invest some unknown amount of cash that now resides in its so-called Treasury General Account in the private repo market, as opposed to being parked at the Fed, as it is now. If the TGA were invested in the repo market, it would earn a return where it does not when it’s placed at the Fed. It could also help bolster repo market liquidity. It would also incur risk from being in private markets. The current size of the TGA stands at just under $1 trillion, and it can be seen as an equivalent of a checkbook for the US Treasury. Cash parked at the TGA is volatile and can move sharply depending on things like tax payment dates and Treasury debt auction settlements. When cash moves out of the TGA it turns into banking sector reserves, and it has implications for how the Fed manages market liquidity and its still large balance sheet. Participants in the New York Fed panel said that while they welcomed the prospect of government cash entering the market, they would appreciate some sort of process to make it predictable and understandable, rather than some random force that impacts market liquidity at unpredictable intervals. This possible policy shift “could be an important stabilizer to the market even if it's not being used every single day,” said Jill Funk, a managing director at J.P. Morgan. Panel participants said if the Treasury were to make the shift in how it uses TGA cash, it would be helpful to conduct operations early in the day, when repo market participants do most of their key trading. The Treasury could also potentially offer a threshold on the TGA where cash would be invested into repo, for example. The TGA has also come under greater attention as the Treasury Department has [USN:L1N4570QL TEXT:"upsized"] debt buyback operations in an attempt to counter rising borrowing costs. That effort has largely foundered, and some have speculated whether the Treasury might use TGA cash to augment its buyback efforts, though that could raise questions about the government paying for its activities by diverting cash from operational needs.

item.title: NY Fed's Perli says monetary policy toolkit working very well
item.description: The Federal Reserve’s monetary policy control toolkit continues to be very effective, Roberto Perli, a New York Fed official responsible for implementing short-term interest rate policy for the central bank, said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Michael Derby
item.content:encoded: The Federal Reserve’s monetary policy control toolkit continues to be very effective, Roberto Perli, a New York Fed official responsible for implementing short-term interest rate policy for the central bank, said on Tuesday. “We have maintained very strong interest rate control, we have kept reserves within the ample range, and our Treasury bill purchases have run smoothly,” Perli said. He is manager of the New York Fed’s System Open Market Account. His comments came from closing remarks at an event held by the New York Fed on Treasury market issues. Perli leads the technical implementation of monetary policy to achieve the Fed’s employment and inflation mandates. He also said recent central bank actions to add liquidity to the financial system, which are currently paused, are not a preset course, suggesting the Fed could again buy Treasury bills if it thought it needed to bolster market liquidity. He also said so-called Reserve Management Purchases of Treasury bills will be adapted to market liquidity needs. When it comes to Treasury bill buying, “the recent decisions to set them at zero are no different in spirit than any of the other decisions the Desk has made since RMPs started in December of last year,” Perli said. The Fed had been buying bills in large quantities to bolster market liquidity levels and to ensure firm control over the federal funds target rate range, the institution’s main tool to achieve its policy goals. It stopped buying recently after concluding the market had the needed amount of liquidity. The buying had been technical in nature and was not designed to provide stimulus to the market, even as the purchases increased the overall size of the Fed’s balance sheet. Perli said in his remarks that the New York Fed has a handle on the factors that govern the RMPs. The New York Fed “process for forecasting reserves is robust and generally quite accurate,” Perli said, adding “forecast misses over the past four years represent a very small fraction of total reserves supply and are easily accommodated by our ample reserves framework.” Perli also said in his remarks that “strictly from a monetary policy implementation perspective, offering a centrally cleared version of our standing repo operations would offer some clear benefits.”

item.title: Venezuelano baleado por agente do ICE está internado tratando paralisia, diz advogada
item.description: Um venezuelano baleado por um agente federal da imigração em Austin, no Texas, que passou a noite detido pelo ICE com uma bala alojada nas costas, está sendo tratado em um hospital devido a uma paralisia do lado esquerdo do corpo, disse sua advogada.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Um venezuelano baleado por um agente federal da imigração em Austin, no Texas, que passou a noite detido pelo ICE com uma bala alojada nas costas, está sendo tratado em um hospital devido a uma paralisia do lado esquerdo do corpo, disse sua advogada. O homem, Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, “foi transferido para outro hospital para receber tratamento para a paralisia no lado esquerdo”, disse a advogada Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch em suas redes sociais na noite de segunda-feira. Lincoln-Goldfinch acrescentou que iria visitá-lo logo na manhã desta terça-feira. Durante uma entrevista coletiva na segunda-feira, Lincoln-Goldfinch apresentou um homem que participou por telefone e se identificou como Perez. Ele disse ter sido transferido no domingo para uma unidade de triagem do Serviço de Imigração e Alfândega dos EUA (ICE), cerca de 210 quilômetros a sudoeste de Austin, depois de passar algumas horas no hospital após o tiroteio. Na ligação de segunda-feira, Perez, de 28 anos, disse que ainda estava sangrando e não estava recebendo atendimento médico adequado. “Não estou bem por causa do tiro que levei”, disse ele em espanhol. Acrescentou que teve que dormir no chão do centro de detenção, mas não explicou o motivo. Ele contou que estava trabalhando como motorista de entrega de comida da DoorDash no domingo quando seu carro foi atingido lateralmente pelos agentes, que, segundo ele, não se identificaram nem acionaram qualquer tipo de luz ou sirene. Perez disse que um agente atirou nele enquanto ele ainda estava dentro do carro e que não houve perseguição a pé. A polícia de Austin afirmou no domingo que ele havia fugido dos agentes. A Promotoria do Condado de Travis solicitou nesta terça-feira que o Departamento de Segurança Interna (DHS) suspendesse o processo de deportação contra Perez enquanto a investigação sobre o tiroteio continuar, alegando que sua capacidade de participar como testemunha relevante seria “gravemente prejudicada” caso ele fosse deportado. O DHS não respondeu aos pedidos de comentário na segunda-feira nem nesta terça-feira. No domingo, o DHS divulgou um comunicado por escrito afirmando que Perez estava ilegalmente nos EUA e que tinha uma ordem definitiva de deportação do país. O órgão não forneceu detalhes sobre as circunstâncias do tiroteio.

item.title: Boeing, GoGo test satellite-linked military drone in challenge to Starlink
item.description: Boeing's drone subsidiary Insitu and aviation Wi-Fi provider Gogo have successfully tested a military drone using satellite communications, the companies said on Tuesday, underscoring growing efforts by governments and defense firms to reduce reliance on Elon Musk's Starlink.
item.dc:creator: Mike Stone
item.content:encoded: Boeing's drone subsidiary Insitu and aviation Wi-Fi provider Gogo have successfully tested a military drone using satellite communications, the companies said on Tuesday, underscoring growing efforts by governments and defense firms to reduce reliance on Elon Musk's Starlink. Gogo Special Missions, the military and government arm of Gogo (GOGO.O) , and Insitu (BA.N) integrated a modified version of Gogo's Galileo HDX antenna onto Insitu's Integrator drone, a mid-sized uncrewed aircraft used by military customers for surveillance and reconnaissance missions. Drone warfare has become central to military strategy following its widespread use in Russia's war in Ukraine and conflicts across the Middle East. As militaries seek to operate drones at longer ranges, withstand jamming attacks and carry out increasingly complex missions, they are turning to satellite networks such as Starlink rather than relying on line-of-sight radio links. Gogo and Insitu said their system would provide the Integrator drone with high-speed global internet through Eutelsat OneWeb's (ETL.PA) low-Earth-orbit satellite network and would not be subject to US International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), easing exports to international customers. "Adding an ITAR-free, high-speed SATCOM option is an essential capability for our global customers," John Kelly, Insitu's vice president of growth, said in a statement, adding that the technology would extend command-and-control range and allow faster transmission of sensor data from the battlefield. Gogo and Insitu did not disclose a timeline for deploying the system. Providing military users with Starlink and Starshield, SpaceX's secure government-focused satellite communications service, has become an important source of revenue for Musk's company. But [USN:L5N3V50JK TEXT:"European governments"] and [USN:L6N41W1B2 TEXT:"some in the Pentagon"] have voiced concerns about an over-reliance on Starlink, whose constellation of thousands of satellites dwarfs those of its rivals.

item.title: Report: Presidents Cup stipends to top $25M
item.description: For the third consecutive Presidents Cup, all participants will be paid $250,000 each, taking the total compensation for competitors over the $25 million mark, Front Office Sports reported Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: For the third consecutive Presidents Cup, all participants will be paid $250,000 each, taking the total compensation for competitors over the $25 million mark, Front Office Sports reported Tuesday. The PGA Tour, which operates the event, started paying players, captains and assistant captains the same amount going back to the 2022 event. Participants were not compensated in the previous 13 events going back to the Presidents Cup debut in 1994. Unlike the Ryder Cup, which pits top players from the United States and Europe, the Presidents Cup is contested among top U.S. players and top players from around the world outside of Europe. This year's Presidents Cup, which begins Thursday and concludes Sunday, will be played at Medinah Country Club just outside of Chicago. The PGA of America started playing U.S. Ryder Cup participants for the first time last year, providing $200,000 to each. The European Tour Group did not compensate its players for Ryder Cup play. The organizers of both the Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup also donate millions to charities each time the events are played. --Field Level Media

item.title: IDB head working on $2.5 billion Venezuela loan, faces board pushback, sources say
item.description: The head of the Inter-American Development Bank is working to secure approval for a $2.5 billion loan for Venezuela but has faced pushback from some members of the lender's board, two sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Campos, Cassandra Garrison
item.content:encoded: The head of the Inter-American Development Bank is working to secure approval for a $2.5 billion loan for Venezuela but has faced pushback from some members of the lender's board, two sources with knowledge of the matter told Reuters. IDB President Ilan Goldfajn has faced concern from the board about lending to Caracas without moves by other multilateral lenders that would ensure Venezuela's capacity to repay, although the board recognizes the benefits of re-engaging with Venezuela, one of the sources said. The IDB declined to comment and the Venezuelan government did not respond to a request for comment. The IDB stopped making new loans to the South American country in May 2018, after it fell behind on payments. Renewed lending would require special approvals, which are not uncommon when countries return to borrowing from multilateral institutions, but the source said some on the board are apprehensive about the rapid pace of the process. The oil exporter has in recent years faced a liquidity and macroeconomic crisis due in large part to much lower oil revenue and a widening fiscal deficit. Analysts expect the restructuring of its debt, which they estimate [USN:L8N42N17D TEXT:"could exceed $200 billion"], to be a slow and convoluted process. Any proposal to lend to Venezuela would ultimately require approval from the IDB's 14-member Executive Board, where the United States wields 30% of the voting power, followed by Argentina and Brazil with 11.35% each. A $2.5 billion IDB operation, while dwarfed by Venezuela's substantial overall debt, would mark a milestone in early-stage recovery financing. The IDB currently cannot issue loans to Venezuela under its public arrears policy, given that Caracas has more than $2 billion in overdue principal and interest with the regional lender. The arrears, however, could be cleared with a third-party bridge loan, a standard process in reintegrating a country into the international financial system, one of the sources said. The proposed IDB loan would fall under a Special Development Lending arrangement, according to the two sources, which in the case of Venezuela would be capped at $500 million as per IDB rules. A $2.5 billion loan to Caracas would require a size waiver, and a second waiver on the lack of a standing program with the International Monetary Fund — an SDL requirement, according to the bank's rules. Goldfajn told Reuters on Monday that the IDB is working on an [USN:L6N45D0U3 TEXT:"“engagement note” with Venezuela"], a short-term plan that typically precedes new lending. The IDB has 48 member countries, including 26 borrowing members in Latin America and the Caribbean, where it is the largest source of multilateral financing. In 2025, it approved $17.4 billion in new loans and guarantees, while its outstanding loan portfolio reached nearly $118 billion, according to its latest annual report.

item.title: Flexible Jacks benefitting from new England role with bat and ball
item.description: Will Jacks has embraced a new position down the batting order that has also seen him take on a more influential role with the ball following career-best One Day International figures of 5-22 in England’s 89-run win over Sri Lanka on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Will Jacks has embraced a new position down the batting order that has also seen him take on a more influential role with the ball following career-best One Day International figures of 5-22 in England’s [USN:L6N45E0YW TEXT:"89-run win over Sri Lanka"] on Tuesday. When Jacks first came into the ODI side in 2023, he mostly batted in the top three and was bowled sparingly, but as England look ahead to the 2027 Cricket World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, his role is evolving. His first 15 ODIs batting mostly higher up the order saw him average 31.20 with the bat and 45.00 with the ball. But since dropping down the order to number 6 or 7, in the last 12 matches he has played his batting average has risen to 42.83 and his bowling average dropped to 34.60. He was a match-winner against Sri Lanka with his five-wicket haul and an unbeaten 46 with the bat, earning praise from captain Harry Brook. "The way he has come into this role in the middle order and played his part with the ball has been awesome," Brook told Sky Sports. Jacks could be particularly well suited to the conditions at next year’s World Cup, having played with success for several seasons in South Africa’s SA20, giving him an understanding of white-ball conditions there. "It is about playing the situation and going into each game with an open mind, see what the situation is and play accordingly," Jacks said. "What we have been doing really well recently is communicating what the pitch is like and what sort of score we would like. Joe and Harry were saying ... 275-280 would be a good score. "When I got out there (to bat), I found it quite difficult and thought it might be a bit lower, but in 50-over cricket you have more time than you think and we could catch up a little bit in the end." Jacks has also previously been used in the opening overs of a bowling innings, but on this occasion came later on. "Having batted on it, I knew I would play a decent role (with the ball). When I bowl does not matter to me, Harry likes to be flexible," he said. The second match in the three-game series will be played in Leeds on Thursday.

item.title: Canada is giving C$100 million in international aid for Palestine, says Carney
item.description: Canada is giving C$100 million in international assistance for Palestine, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canada is giving C$100 million in international assistance for Palestine, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Tuesday. Carney told reporters at the United Nations that C$80 million was for humanitarian aid to alleviate immediate human suffering, and C$20 million was to support peace and security capacity building.

item.title: In UN farewell, Macron denounces Trump's Gaza diplomacy as spectacle of shame
item.description: France's President Emmanuel Macron on Tuesday dismissed US President Donald Trump's claims of having secured peace in Gaza, saying not a single humanitarian corridor had been reopened in the enclave despite the proclaimed peace.
item.dc:creator: John Irish
item.content:encoded: France's President Emmanuel Macron on Tuesday dismissed US President Donald Trump's claims of having secured peace in Gaza, saying not a single humanitarian corridor had been reopened in the enclave despite the proclaimed peace. In his final address to the United Nations before leaving office next year, Macron said the world was witnessing a spectacle that should shame everyone, rebuking Trump's portrayal of his Gaza peace plan as a diplomatic triumph. He spoke at the United Nations General Assembly hours after Trump had from the same rostrum hailed his Gaza peace plan as a diplomatic triumph. "A year ago, here in this very hall, about a dozen states had recognized Palestine. I hear the cynicism of some people: 'Recognition is just a piece of paper, look at the reality,'" Macron said, banging his fist on the podium in his last speech at the United Nations before stepping down next May. "But what credibility do we have if we continue to remain inactive in the face of Gaza? Some boast of a supposed peace. But that peace has not reopened humanitarian access for a single second. Are we simply to stand by and watch this spectacle that should shame us all?" WHITE HOUSE RESPONDS In response to Macron's criticism, White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said: “President Trump ended the war between Israel and Hamas, freed all living hostages, returned the bodies of the deceased to their loved ones, and is now leading the implementation of the 20-Point Plan for Peace in Gaza. While others talk, this President took this complex problem head on. No one has done more for peace and stability in the region.” Macron has faced criticism among some politicians and activists in France that he has done little since recognising a Palestinian state last September. Despite the criticism, Paris has toughened its stance on settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank, imposing some national sanctions and launching a process to ban products from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. "Look at what is happening in the West Bank, where every day violations are committed. In whose name? Hamas has never operated in the West Bank," Macron said. "What is happening there is building, day by day, the impossibility of a project that should be based on respect for the legitimate right of the Palestinian people to exist." France's ties with Israel have been particularly strained over the last year. Macron said those who believed that violating the sovereignty of all of Israel's neighbors would ensure its security were mistaken. "They are weakening Israel's security, both today and in the future," he said. 'LONG LIVE THE UNITED NATIONS' Seven months from France's next presidential election, Macron was making his last appearance after first taking to the rostrum in 2017. Often showing a keen eye for the trappings of diplomacy — the grand settings, the symbolism, the personal connections — he has at the same time failed to translate this into lasting strategic gains, analysts say. However, he has always been a staunch defender of the multilateral system and the United Nations. Macron warned against a global "return to the law of the jungle", saying countries faced a choice between a world governed by power and coercion and a "civilized international society." "Our duty, more than ever, is to stand alongside the United Nations. We cannot accept the new order of impunity that some would like to build," he said. He ended his speech with "Long Live the United Nations!"

item.title: Nasdaq tem fechamento recorde; ações do setor de IA registram alta
item.description: O Nasdaq registrou um fechamento recorde nesta terça-feira, impulsionado pela Micron Technology e outras ações relacionadas à IA, enquanto o S&P 500 ficou um pouco abaixo de sua máxima histórica, com os preços do petróleo oscilando em torno de US$100 por barril.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich, Johann Cherian
item.content:encoded: O Nasdaq registrou um fechamento recorde nesta terça-feira, impulsionado pela Micron Technology e outras ações relacionadas à IA, enquanto o S&P 500 ficou um pouco abaixo de sua máxima histórica, com os preços do petróleo oscilando em torno de US$100 por barril. As ações do setor de chips ampliaram os ganhos recentes, enquanto as ações de software voltadas para o consumidor perderam terreno. Os investidores se concentraram na forte recepção do assistente de IA da Meta, lançado neste mês e capaz de enviar emails e realizar transações em nome do usuário. O sucesso do assistente de IA, chamado Muse, impulsionou os ganhos das ações de chips relacionadas à IA nos últimos dias. No entanto, alguns temiam que ele pudesse competir com varejistas, corretoras online e outras empresas do setor de consumo. A Amazon (AMZN.O) bloqueou, na segunda-feira, o acesso do assistente para compras em sua plataforma. “Há muitas ações do setor de tecnologia em baixa hoje devido a receios relacionados ao Muse, de um tipo ou de outro”, disse Jed Ellerbroek, gestor de portfólio da Argent Capital Management. “As pessoas temem que o Muse seja usado para gerenciar seus contratos de seguro, reservar suas viagens e procurar coisas para comprar.” Os aplicativos de transporte Uber Technologies (UBER.N) e Lyft (LYFT.O) perderam mais de 1% cada, enquanto a Charles Schwab (SCHW.N) tombou 6,1% e a Airbnb (ABNB.O) recuou 3%. A Micron (MU.O) subiu 5% e a Sandisk (SNDK.O) ganhou quase 7%. Os preços do petróleo oscilaram em torno de US$100 o barril, enquanto o rendimento dos títulos do Tesouro de 10 anos de referência oscilou em torno de 4,94% depois que o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, advertiu em um discurso na Assembleia Geral da ONU que poderia “aniquilar a República Islâmica” caso não fosse alcançado um acordo para pôr fim ao conflito no Oriente Médio. Os investidores também aguardavam uma cúpula entre EUA e China na quinta-feira, com os operadores especulando que a trégua comercial com Pequim poderia ser prorrogada e que as negociações poderiam abordar a regulamentação da inteligência artificial. “O que as pessoas esperam é, pelo menos, o início de um diálogo que talvez permita chegar a algum tipo de estrutura global, em vez de ficarem brigando entre si...”, disse Joe Saluzzi, chefe de pesquisa de estrutura do mercado de ações da Themis Trading. O S&P 500 fechou praticamente estável, em 7.764,64 pontos. O Nasdaq subiu 0,45%, para 27.244,28 pontos, seu segundo fechamento recorde consecutivo. O Dow Jones Industrial Average recuou 0,36%, para 51.863,69 pontos. Seis dos 11 índices setoriais do S&P 500 registraram queda, liderados pelo setor financeiro (.SPSY) , com baixa de 1,68%, seguido por uma perda de 0,8% no setor de serviços de comunicação (.SPLRCL) . O S&P 500 ficou menos de 0,5% abaixo de seu recorde de fechamento de 13 de agosto. O JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) e o Wells Fargo (WFC.N) registraram perdas superiores a 3%. A presidente do Federal Reserve de Boston, Susan Collins, afirmou que apoiou o aumento da taxa de juros da semana passada, citando riscos de inflação. O presidente do Fed de Nova York, John Williams, afirmou que a estrutura do Fed para controlar as taxas de curto prazo tem sido eficaz no apoio aos mercados financeiros. Os operadores estimam uma probabilidade de 53% de que o Fed aumente as taxas de juros em pelo menos 25 pontos-base em outubro, segundo a ferramenta FedWatch do CME Group.

item.title: Ibovespa fecha em alta com ajuda de Petrobras em dia "de lado"
item.description: O Ibovespa fechou com alta modesta nesta terça-feira, apoiada pela recuperação das ações da Petrobras, em pregão marcado pela repercussão de nova pesquisa eleitoral e análise da ata da última reunião de política monetária do Banco Central.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: O Ibovespa fechou com alta modesta nesta terça-feira, apoiada pela recuperação das ações da Petrobras, em pregão marcado pela repercussão de nova pesquisa eleitoral e análise da ata da última reunião de política monetária do Banco Central. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) subiu 0,44%, a 187.422,92 pontos, após marcar 184.976,81 na mínima e chegar a 187.671,74 na máxima do dia. O volume financeiro somou R$30,23 bilhões. De acordo com o responsável pela mesa de ações e sócio do BTG Pactual, Jerson Zanlorenzi, a bolsa ficou praticamente "de lado", sem grandes variações, sem grandes destaques. Zanlorenzi chamou a atenção para o cenário eleitoral, principalmente a proximidade do primeiro turno, em 4 de outubro, que deixa investidores "em compasso de espera", principalmente após uma performance positiva recente. Em setembro, o Ibovespa acumula valorização de 5,64%, em parte ajudada pelo retorno do investidor estrangeiro. De acordo com dados da B3, o saldo de capital externo está positivo em R$9,23 bilhões no mês até o dia 18. Sob os holofotes no dia, nova [USN:L6N45D10W TEXT:"pesquisa Quaest"], conhecida na véspera, referendou o cenário de disputa acirrada entre o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) pelo Palácio do Planalto. Investidores aguardam novos levantamentos na semana. O Banco Central também divulgou mais cedo a [USN:L1N45E0BL TEXT:"ata"] da última reunião de política monetária, que manteve o tom do comunicado que acompanhou a decisão da semana passada de reduzir a Selic a 13,75% ao ano. A Assembleia Geral das Nações Unidas, em Nova York, também ocupou as atenções, com discursos do [USN:S0N43107H TEXT:"presidente Lula"] e do seu par norte-americano, Donald Trump, na primeira etapa da sessão. Havia expectativas de que o evento corroborasse um avanço diplomático envolvendo a guerra no Irã. À tarde, Trump disse que autoridades dos EUA tiveram uma reunião “[USN:L6N45E0XM TEXT:"muito boa"]” de três horas nesta terça-feira com a delegação iraniana. O barril do petróleo Brent recuou 1,09%, a US$99,25 tendo ainda como pano de fundo que o Irã sinalizou que poderá reabrir o Estreito de Ormuz em sete dias e que a Arábia Saudita se prepara para retomar as exportações de seu porto de Yanbu, no Mar Vermelho. Em Nova York, o índice acionário S&P 500 (.SPX) terminou estável, enquanto o rendimento do título de 10 anos do Tesouro norte-americano marcava 4,9511% no final do dia, de 4,963% na véspera. DESTAQUES PETROBRAS PN avançou 0,73% e PETROBRAS ON (PETR3.SA) subiu 0,61%, mesmo com o declínio do petróleo no exterior. A diretora de Engenharia, Tecnologia e Inovação da Petrobras, Renata Baruzzi, afirmou nesta terça-feira que a companhia enviará uma [USN:L1N45E0II TEXT:"sonda"] de perfuração à Bacia da Foz do Amazonas em janeiro para iniciar os trabalhos em três novos poços. ITAÚ PN subiu 0,23%, também revertendo a fraqueza de parte do pregão, em dia misto no setor. BRADESCO PN avançou 1,49% e BTG PACTUAL UNIT valorizou-se 0,71%, mas BANCO DO BRASIL ON (BBAS3.SA) recuou 1,39% e SANTANDER BRASIL UNIT cedeu 0,6%, com novos avanços relacionados à oferta de troca feita pelo seu controlador, o espanhol Santander (SAN.MC) , para a aquisição das ações em circulação da subsidiária brasileira. VALE ON (VALE3.SA) fechou em alta 0,39%, resistindo à queda dos futuros do [USN:L6N45E0JQ TEXT:"minério de ferro"] na China, pressionados por perspectivas fracas de demanda no curto prazo. A Vale também confirmou nesta terça-feira a [USN:L1N45E0CY TEXT:"aquisição"] de uma participação de 30% na mineradora Ligga S.A., por meio de aporte de capital de aproximadamente US$190 milhões, e a assinatura de um contrato de compra de minério de ferro sinter feed produzido pela empresa. SUZANO ON (SUZB3.SA) encerrou com acréscimo de 2,81%, em meio a notícias sobre [USN:L1N45E0T5 TEXT:"reajuste"] nos preços da celulose em outubro. A companhia está comunicando a clientes na Ásia uma elevação de US$20 a tonelada, enquanto para as Américas e Europa o preço será elevado em US$50. AXIA ON (AXIA3.SA) fechou em alta de 1,27%, tendo no radar notícia de que o conselho de administração aprovou uma nova operação de [USN:S0N44L00L TEXT:"resgate"] de ações preferenciais classe C (PNC) envolvendo 70.716.228 papéis, equivalentes a R$3,9 bilhões e a 15,46% dessa classe de ação. Os resgates de PNCs funcionam como uma espécie de programa de recompra pela Axia. VIVARA ON (VIVA3.SA) perdeu 4,37%, em sessão de ajustes, após duas altas seguidas, sendo que apenas na véspera o papel subiu quase 5,5%.

item.title: Microsoft to keep shareholder proposal rights through 2027, even as SEC reduces oversight
item.description: Microsoft will consider shareholder proposals at its annual meetings through next year, at the request of an activist looking to preserve investor rights as they come under pressure from a contentious U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission rule change proposed last week.
item.dc:creator: Ross Kerber
item.content:encoded: Microsoft (MSFT.O) will consider shareholder proposals at its annual meetings through next year, at the request of an activist looking to preserve investor rights as they come under pressure from a contentious U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission [USN:L1N4580J4 TEXT:"rule change proposed last week"]. Under an agreement with conservative activist Paul Chesser, seen by Reuters, Microsoft will continue to apply existing thresholds for investors to submit resolutions for a vote, even as the SEC considers changes that critics say would sideline individual investors, religious groups, unions and others who have had a say through the shareholder proposal process for decades. The agreement only lasts a year, but could effectively offset efforts by the regulatory agency to shift power away from investors to corporate executives. Chesser said he hopes Microsoft's approach will become a corporate-governance model to assure mom-and-pop investors a voice that can be followed by other companies. "Microsoft put in writing that the smallest long-term owners of the company will still have a way to be heard next year, no matter what the SEC does," said Chesser, director at the National Legal and Policy Center. "Every other company that claims to value its shareholders should be asked why it won't do the same," he said. In an e-mailed statement, a Microsoft spokesperson said: "With the Securities and Exchange Commission announcing that its shareholder proposal regulatory framework is under review, we agreed to maintain the current eligibility thresholds for one year, providing Microsoft and its shareholders a clear and predictable process for the next proxy cycle." Shareholder resolutions on topics like climate change, workforce diversity and executive pay have become the focus of many shareholder meetings in recent years, although many have received [USN:L1N3T70QY TEXT:"diminishing support"] from major fund firms. EARLY EXAMPLE Microsoft's meeting is set for December 8 and traditionally has been held early in the proxy cycle that runs through June 30 of each year, bringing attention to the company's governance procedures. Last week SEC Chair Paul Atkins, an appointee of US President Donald Trump, proposed to end the agency's oversight of the resolutions process and [USN:L1N4580J4 TEXT:"move the function to state officials"], which activists saw as a shift that would diminish their influence. The move is part of a broader [USN:L1N3P40X7 TEXT:"shift of power"] away from investors toward managers by the Republican-dominated commission. The agreement between Chesser and Microsoft, seen by Reuters, says Microsoft will continue to apply previous eligibility requirements for investors to submit resolutions for a vote. Chesser's group has similar resolutions pending with Procter & Gamble and Oracle (ORCL.N) and may submit more. P&G's annual meeting is set for October 13. In its proxy statement dated August 28, the company recommended votes against the proposal, among other things calling it premature since the SEC hadn't yet proposed its rulemaking. A P&G representative declined to comment. Oracle's AGM has not yet been set. A representative did not immediately respond to questions.

item.title: Trump compromete "poder militar incomparable" contra los cárteles en América
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump se comprometió el martes a reafirmar el dominio de Estados Unidos en el hemisferio occidental y a usar un "poderío militar sin igual" contra las amenazas en la región, al tiempo que reunía a sus aliados en torno a una campaña cada vez más amplia contra los cárteles de la droga.
item.dc:creator: Simon Lewis
item.content:encoded: El presidente Donald Trump se comprometió el martes a reafirmar el dominio de Estados Unidos en el hemisferio occidental y a usar un "poderío militar sin igual" contra las amenazas en la región, al tiempo que reunía a sus aliados en torno a una campaña cada vez más amplia contra los cárteles de la droga. En su intervención ante los líderes mundiales en la Asamblea General de la ONU, Trump calificó a los cárteles de la droga como "el ISIS del hemisferio occidental" e instó a dar una respuesta más contundente a la delincuencia transnacional. Más tarde, en la sede de la ONU, Trump se reunió con los líderes y ministros de Asuntos Exteriores de 14 países de América Latina y el Caribe que se han sumado al "Escudo de las Américas", una coalición contra los cárteles puesta en marcha por su Gobierno. Trump instó al grupo a unirse a Estados Unidos para calificar a 24 grupos de narcotraficantes como amenazas para la estabilidad e imponerles sanciones. Posteriormente, los países emitieron un comunicado en el que se comprometían a tomar medidas para aplicar dichas sanciones conjuntas. La incursión estadounidense que condujo a la captura del líder venezolano Nicolás Maduro y el posterior acuerdo petrolero con el Gobierno interino pusieron de manifiesto la voluntad de Estados Unidos de actuar en la región, dijo Trump ante los líderes mundiales en la Asamblea General. "Nuestras acciones en Venezuela son prueba de que Estados Unidos ya no permitirá que las amenazas a América se afiancen en ningún lugar del hemisferio occidental y, si es necesario, utilizaremos nuestro poderío militar sin igual para salvaguardar los intereses nacionales vitales de Estados Unidos", afirmó. La Estrategia de Seguridad Nacional de Trump, presentada a finales del año pasado, estableció planes para una versión renovada de la Doctrina Monroe, la política del siglo XIX que reivindicaba la primacía de Estados Unidos en todo el continente americano y que los críticos han asociado durante mucho tiempo con décadas de intervención estadounidense. El propio Trump ha empezado a llamarla la "Doctrina Donroe", un juego de palabras con su propio nombre, después de que la expresión se popularizó en los medios conservadores. Aun así, la atención que Trump presta al hemisferio occidental ha suscitado temores de un proyecto neocolonial. El presidente brasileño, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, en su discurso ante la ONU, se mostró indignado ante este enfoque y advirtió a los países de América Latina y el Caribe de las "renovadas tentaciones hegemónicas". "Brasil no es el patio trasero de nadie", dijo Lula. La coalición "Escudo de las Américas" incluye gobiernos estrechamente alineados con Trump, entre ellos los de Argentina, Ecuador y El Salvador, cuyos líderes han sido elogiados o respaldados por Trump como candidatos. Colombia y Perú se unieron después de que, en los últimos meses, asumieron el poder presidentes alineados con Trump. Brasil y México se encuentran entre los países que no se han sumado.

item.title: Macron denuncia en la ONU la diplomacia de Trump en Gaza como un "espectáculo vergonzoso"
item.description: El presidente de Francia, Emmanuel Macron, desestimó el martes las afirmaciones del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de haber logrado la paz en Gaza, señalando que no se había reabierto ni un solo corredor humanitario en el enclave a pesar de la paz proclamada.
item.dc:creator: John Irish
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Francia, Emmanuel Macron, desestimó el martes las afirmaciones del presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, de haber logrado la paz en Gaza, señalando que no se había reabierto ni un solo corredor humanitario en el enclave a pesar de la paz proclamada. En su último discurso ante las Naciones Unidas antes de dejar el cargo el año que viene, Macron dijo que el mundo estaba siendo testigo de un espectáculo que debería avergonzarle, y criticó la forma en que Trump había presentado su plan de paz para Gaza como un triunfo diplomático. Habló ante la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidas horas después de que Trump, desde la misma tribuna, aclamó su plan de paz para Gaza como un triunfo diplomático. "Hace un año, aquí mismo, en esta misma sala, cerca de una docena de Estados habían reconocido a Palestina. Oigo el cinismo de algunas personas: 'El reconocimiento no es más que un trozo de papel, miren la realidad'", dijo Macron, golpeando con el puño el atril en su último discurso ante Naciones Unidas antes de dejar el cargo el próximo mes de mayo. "Pero, ¿qué credibilidad tenemos si seguimos sin actuar ante la situación de Gaza? Algunos se jactan de una supuesta paz. Pero esa paz no ha reabierto el acceso humanitario ni un solo segundo. ¿Vamos a quedarnos simplemente de brazos cruzados viendo este espectáculo que debería avergonzarnos a todos?". La Casa Blanca no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. "Hace un año, cuando me dirigí a los grandes líderes en esta sala, la guerra en Gaza aún se libraba con brutalidad", había dicho Trump en su discurso. "Unas semanas más tarde, pusimos fin a la guerra en Gaza, salvando miles y miles de vidas". Macron ha sido objeto de críticas por parte de algunos políticos y activistas franceses, que le reprochan haber hecho muy poco desde que reconoció al Estado palestino en septiembre del año pasado. A pesar de las críticas, París ha endurecido su postura ante la violencia de los colonos contra los palestinos en Cisjordania, imponiendo algunas sanciones nacionales y poniendo en marcha un proceso para prohibir los productos procedentes de los asentamientos israelíes de la Cisjordania ocupada.
